title: Lipid Mediator Profiling of Human M1- and M2-Macrophages During Host-Pathogen Interactions
author: Günther, Ehrhardt, et al.
materials: Zeiss Axiovert 25 inverted phase contrast microscope

steps.title: Prepare dextran/PBS mixture
steps.instruction: Place 10 mL of 5 % dextran solution and 10 mL sterile PBS into each of two 50 mL Falcon tubes, then add 20 mL blood to each tube (total 40 mL per tube).

steps.title: Sediment erythrocytes
steps.instruction: Shake the tubes gently, open the lids and let the mixture stand for 40 min at 20 °C to allow erythrocytes to sediment.

steps.title: Layer onto Histopaque and centrifuge
steps.instruction: Prepare two 50 mL Falcon tubes each containing 10 mL Histopaque. Carefully pipette the supernatant from the dextran/blood mixture onto the Histopaque without mixing, then centrifuge at 2 000 rpm (870 × g) for 10 min at 20 °C without brake (Heraeus Multifuge X3R).

steps.title: Isolate PBMC ring
steps.instruction: Using a pipette, collect the white PBMC ring located between the two liquid phases from each tube, combine into a fresh 50 mL Falcon tube, and keep the cells on ice.

steps.title: Wash PBMCs
steps.instruction: Wash the PBMCs twice with ice‑cold PBS:

substeps.instruction: Fill to 50 mL with ice‑cold PBS and centrifuge at 1 200 rpm (314 × g) for 10 min at 4 °C.
Discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 5 mL ice‑cold PBS, fill to 50 mL, centrifuge at 1 200 rpm (314 × g) for 5 min at 4 °C. Repeat this wash once more.
Finally discard supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 5 mL ice‑cold PBS.

steps.title: Count and seed PBMCs
steps.instruction: Count cells (average 4.6 × 10⁸ PBMC per leukocyte pack) using a Vi‑Cell XR (1:50 dilution). Seed 1.8 × 10⁸ cells into a 175 cm² flask with 15 mL PBS+/+. Allow cells to adhere for 1 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Remove non‑adherent cells and wash
steps.instruction: Gently remove the PBS+/+ containing non‑adherent cells and wash the flask with 10 mL pre‑warmed (37 °C) PBS, pouring the liquid onto the side of the flask (do not add directly onto cells).

steps.title: Add differentiation medium
steps.instruction: Add 15 mL pre‑warmed RPMI macrophage medium to the flask, then add either 60 µL of 5 µg/mL GM‑CSF stock (final 20 ng/mL) for M0‑GM‑CSF or 60 µL of 5 µg/mL M‑CSF stock (final 20 ng/mL) for M0‑M‑CSF.

steps.title: Incubate and refresh medium
steps.instruction: Incubate the cells at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂. After 3 days, discard the medium and add fresh RPMI medium containing the same cytokine concentration.

steps.title: Detach M0 macrophages
steps.instruction: After 6 days, discard medium and wash cells with 10 mL pre‑warmed (37 °C) PBS. Add 15 mL pre‑warmed PBS‑EDTA, incubate 20 min at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂. Tap flasks gently, rinse with PBS‑EDTA, and collect cells into a 50 mL Falcon tube. Add 10 mL pre‑warmed PBS, scrape remaining cells, and collect the suspension.

steps.title: Centrifuge and count M0 cells
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the cell suspension at 1 200 rpm (314 × g) for 10 min at 20 °C. Discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 1 mL RPMI macrophage medium, and count cells (Vi‑Cell XR, 1:10 dilution).

steps.title: Seed M0 cells for polarization
steps.instruction: Seed the counted M0 cells into the appropriate plate format according to Table 1 (e.g., 2 × 10⁶ cells in 2 mL for a 6‑well plate). Allow cells to attach for at least 1 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Polarize to M1 or M2
steps.instruction: Add polarization mix:

substeps.instruction: For M0‑GM‑CSF → M1: add freshly prepared mix to achieve final 100 ng/mL LPS and 20 ng/mL IFN‑γ; incubate 24 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.
For M0‑M‑CSF → M2: add mix to achieve final 20 ng/mL IL‑4; incubate 48 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Add inhibitors or stimuli
steps.instruction: For long‑term incubations, add the desired inhibitor or stimulating agent (typically 30 min before adding polarization medium). Keep DMSO concentration below 0.1 % of total medium volume.

steps.title: Prepare live S. aureus culture
steps.instruction: Streak S. aureus (wild‑type 6850 or USA300) on Columbia agar with 5 % sheep blood, incubate upside down 24 h at 37 °C. Pick a single colony into 30 mL brain‑heart infusion (BHI) broth in an Erlenmeyer flask, shake 24 h at 37 °C, 210 rpm.

steps.title: Generate log‑phase S. aureus suspension
steps.instruction: Measure OD₆₀₀ of the overnight culture (blank with BHI). Inoculate fresh 30 mL BHI to an OD of 0.05, shake 4 h at 37 °C, 210 rpm. Centrifuge 15 mL of this culture at 5 300 rpm (3 016 × g) for 3 min at 20 °C. Discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 1 mL PBS (±), and dilute to OD₆₀₀ = 1 (PBS blank).

steps.title: Prepare live E. coli culture
steps.instruction: Streak E. coli (serotype O6:K2:H1) on nutrient‑broth agar, incubate upside down 12 h at 37 °C. Pick a single colony into 30 mL nutrient‑broth (NB) medium, shake 24 h at 37 °C, 210 rpm.

steps.title: Generate log‑phase E. coli suspension
steps.instruction: Measure OD₆₀₀ (blank with NB). Inoculate fresh 30 mL NB to OD 0.05, shake 3 h at 37 °C, 210 rpm. Centrifuge 15 mL at 5 300 rpm (3 016 × g) for 3 min at 20 °C. Discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 1 mL PBS (±), and dilute to OD₆₀₀ = 1.

steps.title: Propagate Influenza A virus
steps.instruction: Seed MDCK cells in 15 cm plates one day prior to reach 80‑90 % confluence. Remove medium, wash once with PBS. Inoculate with low MOI (0.01–0.001) of IAV in PBS‑INF (3–5 mL) for 30 min–1 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂. Remove inoculum, add 13–15 mL EMEM‑INF, and incubate 48–52 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ until cytopathic effect is visible.

steps.title: Harvest and store IAV stock
steps.instruction: Swirl plates and gently pipette medium to collect virus, centrifuge at 4 400 × g for 10 min at 4 °C, collect supernatant, aliquot and store at –80 °C (avoid repeated freeze‑thaw). Use Panserin‑INF instead of EMEM‑INF if needed.

steps.title: Determine IAV titer
steps.instruction: Perform a standard plaque assay as described by Karakus et al.; vortex each dilution gently and use a fresh pipette tip for each step.

steps.title: Thaw IAV aliquots
steps.instruction: Slowly thaw virus aliquots on ice for 30 min–1 h (depending on volume) before infection experiments.

steps.title: Prepare S. aureus conditioned medium
steps.instruction: Repeat steps 13–15 (live S. aureus culture up to log‑phase centrifugation) and collect the supernatant. Sterile‑filter the supernatant through a 0.22 µm filter. Store at 4 °C (do not freeze); use within 2 weeks.

description: The presented protocol has been developed for broad analysis of human monocyte-derived macrophage (MDM) phenotyping and lipid mediator (LM) profiling after host-pathogen interactions. To generate human MDMs, leukocyte concentrates derived from freshly withdrawn blood (16 I.E. heparin/mL blood) of healthy adult male and female volunteers (18–65 years, without details about ancestry, race or ethnicity) were provided, according to guidelines and regulations for working with human material. All steps were performed in a cell culture lab under sterile conditions. This protocol is standardized for high yield isolation of MDMs from different blood donations of the same day. For cell isolation, we prefer using electronic pipettors for time-saving handling. The used solutions and consumables, if not stated otherwise, were all sterile or sterilized via autoclaving. For preparation of all pathogens and pathogen components authorization is needed to handle the pathogens according to the guidelines and laws in your country.
